source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, General Information and Lubrication, p.0-7

procedures.title: Lifting the Corvette on a hoist or jack
steps: Use the shaded areas in figure 9 in the manual as hoist or jack contact points.
Single-post hoist: contact the frame side rails behind the front kick-up and ahead of the #3 body mount at the rear.
Twin-post hoist, no rear axle or suspension work planned: use suspension adapters or drive-on adapters at the front and drive-on adapters at the rear.
If axle work turns out to be needed, put jack stands under the frame side rails on both sides, then lower the rear post.
Twin-post hoist, rear axle work planned: use suspension adapters or drive-on adapters at the front and frame lift adapters at the rear (see figure 10 in the manual).
Without frame lift adapters, use jack stands instead.
notes: The frame lift adapter is a steel beam with wooden blocks bolted on top; the blocks let the beam clear the exhaust system.
